transcript.question: Is Cameron Coscia's aggressive waiver management (9 pickups, most in the league) smart roster-building, or a sign he's papering over a Stinky Faggots roster that's underperforming?

hotSeat.why: Nina Sharpe is favorite on them (+72), Curtis Vaughn is neutral on them (+9)

sides.mel-diaper: The board says Cameron Coscia is fixing real holes on the cheap — he grabbed Cam Skattebo for $16 and got a 24.1-point week out of it, that's process working.
sides.reggie-banks: The scoreboard says The Stinky Faggots are 5-3 with 1094.2 points, fourth place, and no amount of waiver churn changes that he's not separating from the pack this season.

turns.speaker: curtis-vaughn
turns.text: Good evening. The Stinky Faggots sit 5-3, fourth in these standings, and Cameron Coscia has made nine waiver pickups this year, more than anyone else in this league. So here's the question for the desk: is Cameron Coscia building a roster the smart way, or is he just burning FAAB to paper over a team that's actually underperforming its own board? Mel, you're up first.

turns.speaker: mel-diaper
turns.text: SMART. NEXT QUESTION. Cam Skattebo was PICK 146 — ONE FORTY-SIX — and he's the No. 10 running back on this board at 113.8 points. NINE PICKUPS AND HE STILL HAS $76 OF $100 LEFT. That's not papering over a goddamn thing, that's a No. 4 seed built for twenty-four bucks. The Stinky Faggots beat GLORY ASSHOLE in Week 9. Write it down.

claim.text: The Stinky Faggots beat GLORY ASSHOLE in Week 9

turns.speaker: reggie-banks
turns.text: Cute draft. Now look at the scoreboard: 5-3, 1094.2 points, FOURTH. Twelve fewer points than GLORY ASSHOLE, eighty-one behind Chodie mcgruber. Nine pickups and the man's still stuck in the pack. Week 8 they scored 116.9 and lost by 6.1 to a team that started its kicker for 17. GLORY ASSHOLE beats The Stinky Faggots in Week 9 — Saquon Barkley just went for 33.4 and Jordan Love 31.3. Wire adds don't out-scale that. Scoreboard.

claim.text: GLORY ASSHOLE beats The Stinky Faggots in Week 9

turns.speaker: mel-diaper
turns.text: FOURTH?! You're grading a roster on SEED?! Week 6: Bijan Robinson 35.8, Rico Dowdle 33.9, Cam Skattebo 31.0 — ONE HUNDRED POINTS from three backs, 185.4, a 45-point win. Dowdle came off the WIRE. And Week 8 the bench was 19.7 — NINETEEN POINT SEVEN. That's a finished goddamn lineup, not churn. WHERE'S THE PAPER, REGGIE?! Nina, grade it.

managerMentions.evidence: That's a finished goddamn lineup, not churn.

turns.speaker: nina-sharpe
turns.text: Class. The claim is "finished lineup, not churn." Partial credit. Week 6 bench was 39.7, not nineteen — that's a different week you're quoting. Week 8 bench was 19.7, that part's supported. Nine pickups, $76 of $100 left. Both true. Neither proves the other.

turns.speaker: reggie-banks
turns.text: Thank you, Nina. And listen to what else the scoreboard says: Week 7, The Stinky Faggots put up 105.4 at HOME and lost by 11.3 to IR Squad. A.J. Brown went for 28.1 and it still wasn't enough. That's the ceiling problem — one big week in six, and 1094.2 points total. Mel's grade card is horseshit. Nine adds, fourth place. I'll wait.

managerMentions.evidence: That's the ceiling problem — one big week in six, and 1094.2 points total.

turns.speaker: walt-brennan
turns.text: The record only goes back to this season, so I'll speak to what's in front of me: Week 5, Bijan Robinson and Rico Dowdle carried a 146-point week that already had wire fingerprints on it, and this week's 105.4 still lost by 11.3. Nine pickups didn't fix the ceiling. I'd call the churn real and the fourth-place finish honest — Reggie's closer to right, and I'm tired of watching volume get mistaken for a plan.

turns.speaker: mel-diaper
turns.text: CEILING PROBLEM?! Cam Skattebo, PICK 146, is the No. 10 back on this board at 113.8. Khalil Shakir went 20.8 in Week 8 and Jaylen Waddle 20.9. Dex, is any of that churn even in the log?
